title: A man wants to eat every animal on Earth

paragraphs: In the 1830s, William Buckland, a prominent British scientist, hosted unique dinner parties where he served exotic dishes like a mouse on toast.

Despite his eccentricities, Buckland made significant contributions to geology and paleontology. He became the first person to study geology at the University of Oxford. He challenged traditional beliefs, including the biblical account of the Great Flood, by examining fossils. Buckland’s discoveries, such as the Megalosaurus, helped advance the understanding of dinosaurs and evolution. His wife Mary also played a crucial role in their scientific endeavors.
Although Buckland’s dream to eat every animal on Earth remained unfulfilled, his unconventional approach to science demonstrated that scientific exploration could be both rigorous and enjoyable.

words.d: different from what is usual or from the way most people do things

paragraphs: William Buckland was a famous British scientist. In the 1830s, he hosted strange dinner parties. He served unusual foods, like a mouse on toast.

Buckland had unusual habits but he studied geology at Oxford University and he became a respected person in science. He wanted to change old ways of thinking and ideas in the Bible, by studying fossils. Buckland discovered the Megalosaurus bones, which helped people understand dinosaurs better. His wife Mary also loved science and supported his work.
Buckland wanted to eat every animal on Earth. He didn’t manage to do that, but he showed that science can be exciting and fun.
